chunks: Al-Kafi: From him, from Ahmad ibn Ishaq who said:

I wrote to Abi al-Hasan the Third (peace be upon him) asking him about the vision (of God) and the differences of people regarding it, so he wrote: Vision is not valid unless there is air between the viewer and the viewed that the eye can penetrate. If the air is cut off between the viewer and the viewed, vision does not become valid, and this entails confusion/likening, because whenever the viewer equals the viewed in the cause necessitated between them for vision, confusion becomes obligatory, and that is likening (anthropomorphism), because causes must necessarily be connected to their effects.
ai.seo_question: What is the condition for the validity of seeing God according to Imam al-Rida in al-Kafi?
ai.summary: In this hadith from Al-Kafi, Imam al-Rida (peace be upon him) clarifies that visual perception requires a tangible medium like air to connect the viewer and the viewed; without it, vision is invalid. This condition implies a form of likening (anthropomorphism) because the viewer and the viewed share a common causal condition, linking causes to effects.

en.ammaar-muslim: 2. [2/231] al-Kafi: From him (Ahmad b. Idris) from Ahmad b. Ishaq who said:

I wrote to Abi al-Hasan the Third عليه السلام asking him about the vision (of God) and the differences of people about that - he wrote: Vision is impossible when there is no air between the viewer and the viewed. Air which the eye can penetrate through. If there is no air between the viewer and the viewed - vision cannot take place. And this (needing air in between) would entail likening (Allah to His creatures). Because whenever the viewer becomes equivalent with the viewed in terms of sharing the condition necessary for vision between them (to occur) then they would necessarily be alike (in some manner) and that would be anthropomorphism. For causes are necessarily linked to effects.
